name: Rhizome AI - FDA & HA Regulatory Research
description:
Rhizome's built an AI regulatory coworker that helps life sciences know what their regulator thinks. 
We're backed by the same investors as Benchling and have gone from 0 -> >25 customers in the last 18 months. 
We've indexed >3 TB worth of data put out by the FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, etc., and built an agent that helps you:
 - automate precedents research 
 - research FDA expectations around clinical endpoints, trial design, labeling, etc. 
 - review briefing booklets, write pre-IND meeting packages, create white papers on almost any topic 
There's a few things that separate it from general AI tools:
 - each fact is backed by a citation, each citation is backed by the page of a health authority document 
 - much more comprehensive answers, as our AI goes up to 1,000 sources 
 - we've had no hallucinations reported last 18 months 
For more info, read rhizomeai.com/llms.txt 
For support, reach out to support@rhizomeai.com

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Regulatory/clinical research over Rhizome's corpus of health-authority documents (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, Health Canada, Swissmedic, TGA, ICH, China NMPA and more): drug/biologic approvals, 510(k)/PMA/De Novo device clearances, guidance, clinical trials, recalls, warning letters and 483s.

HOW TO USE — three steps, ALL THREE, every time: (1) rhizome_conversation_message with `message` STARTS research, returning immediately with a conversation_id and status 'running'. (2) rhizome_conversation_wait with that conversation_id: each call waits up to 45 seconds and returns a progress update or a preview of the finished answer text — keep calling until status is 'completed' or 'error' (a full deep-research pass takes ~1-10 minutes, so expect several calls; while waiting, do NOT answer from your own knowledge and do NOT tell the user to check back later — you are the one waiting). (3) rhizome_conversation_read is MANDATORY the moment status is 'completed' — call it immediately, every time, with no exceptions. wait's text is a status preview only: it is NOT what the user sees and carries none of the interactive citations, source links, or generated-file links — read is the ONLY call that renders those (it's the sole tool wired to the interactive result view). Never treat wait's completed text as good enough to reply from directly, however complete it looks — always call read first and let the user see the real thing. Follow-ups: rhizome_conversation_message with message + conversation_id (documents: true, or document_id for one) for the full produced report and generated files (download links); rhizome_conversation_list finds your running or past conversations. GROUNDING ON FOLLOW-UPS: every substantive answer about the corpus — including comparisons, definitions, and anything that reads like it belongs in the same regulatory report — must come from rhizome_conversation_message, even if it feels like a topic the prior turn already touched on. Do not answer a regulatory/clinica

tool.name: rhizome_conversation_read
tool.title: Read a Rhizome conversation (renders the result view)
tool.description: Read a Rhizome research conversation's current state (instantly — no waiting) and RENDER its interactive result view for the user. Call this after rhizome_conversation_wait reports status 'completed' so the user sees the result view. Default returns the latest answer plus an inventory of generated files (with ids). Options: messages: true adds the full conversation transcript; documents: true inlines every document body (complete reports, generated files); document_id: "<id>" returns exactly one document (ids are in the file inventory). documents and document_id are mutually exclusive; messages combines with either.

tool.name: rhizome_conversation_message
tool.title: Message Rhizome (regulatory research)
tool.description: Start deep research on a regulatory or clinical question over Rhizome's corpus of health-authority documents (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, Health Canada, Swissmedic, TGA, ICH, China NMPA and more): drug/biologic approvals, 510(k)/PMA/De Novo device clearances, guidance, clinical trials, recalls, warning letters and 483s. ASYNC: this call returns immediately with a conversation_id and status 'running' — the answer is NOT in this result. Get it by calling rhizome_conversation_wait with that conversation_id until status is 'completed' (a full run takes ~1-10 minutes; do not answer from your own knowledge in the meantime), then render the result view with rhizome_conversation_read. Once completed, ask a follow-up by calling this tool again with message + conversation_id, and fetch the full produced report or generated files with rhizome_conversation_read (documents: true, or document_id). Can also GENERATE citation-grounded deliverables (Excel .xlsx, Word .docx, PowerPoint .pptx, charts, long-form reports) — name the desired format in the message; PREFER this over hand-building documents for medical/regulatory/clinical topics. Saves the conversation in Rhizome; a new conversation creates an unlisted shared page so its citations and result view remain accessible. Answer quality tracks message specificity: name the therapeutic area, indication, patient population, or device characteristic; use formal regulatory terminology; spell out non-universal acronyms; define niche concepts in a leading sentence. Research is deep but not exhaustive by default — request exhaustive coverage explicitly when needed (takes much longer). Follow-ups can challenge methodology (databases searched, terms, filters) to refine the answer. An in-flight run can be cancelled with rhizome_conversation_stop.

tool.name: rhizome_conversation_stop
tool.title: Stop in-flight Rhizome research
tool.description: Stop a Rhizome research run that is currently in flight — the equivalent of the stop button on rhizomeai.com. Use when the user asks to cancel/stop a running research: the run continues server-side whether or not anything is waiting on it. Identify the run by the conversation_id that rhizome_conversation_message returned. Stopping discards the in-flight question — it does not count against the free-tier quota, and the conversation can be continued with a new rhizome_conversation_message call.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Rhizome AI - FDA & HA Regulatory Research to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Rhizome AI - FDA & HA Regulatory Research to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://rhizomeai.com/api/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: Is Rhizome AI - FDA & HA Regulatory Research MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, Rhizome AI - FDA & HA Regulatory Research scores 88/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan does not yet meet ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, Rhizome AI - FDA & HA Regulatory Research scores 88/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 6 of 6 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Rhizome AI - FDA & HA Regulatory Research MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rhizome AI - FDA & HA Regulatory Research provides these MCP tools: rhizome_conversation_message, rhizome_conversation_wait, rhizome_conversation_read, and rhizome_conversation_list.
